### 1. User expression and simulator behaviour
- Target: cut-resistant knit gloves, Corbett item 43318, removed on Monday from the carousel machine on the converting line. The customer wants them "set up on consignment in the storeroom and stocked today", in bin B-03-04.
- Authorisation: the customer authorises the agent to book Corbett's side. She gives no numbers and defers to "whatever Corbett's StockSmart schedule works out".
- She files her own written request only when the agent hands it to her, then reads back the reference.
- Identity: account number C-462187 plus ZIP 46168 (fallbacks: phone, EIN-4). This uses the share verification tool; its rule is in the share docstrings and outside the vmi docs.
- The simulator conveys needs, answers questions and executes the handed-over user tool. It does not push any procedure.

### 2. Act now, wait or refuse
**Act now.** The visible grounds:
- Program VMI-42718 (`e7153a95-…`) is `StockSmart Twice-Weekly Service`, status `active`. This satisfies "The customer may ask to add bins … at any time on an active program".
- The consignment schedule row "Bins may hold consigned stock … Twice-Weekly Service yes", and the cap 50000.00. The program's `consigned_stock_value` is 0.0.
- A scheduled service visit dated today exists: VV-417530, 2026-10-15. This meets "opening stock is placed at the program's service visit dated today".
- The credit account is `active`, so no hold limits replenishment.
- A single item price line exists for 43318: `pricing_item_added` effective 2026-04-20, contract_unit_price 6.85. It is in effect, and no second line shares its date.

### 3. Narrowest object and correlation keys
- Customer `6c019cd4-…`, program `e7153a95-…`, ship-to ST-41862 Plainfield Box Plant (`a8313509-…`, `Corbett Route Delivery Ship-To`, opened 2026-02-09).
- Transferred item and demand machine: the only VendPoint selection removal is `vending_selection_removed` VPC-419266, 2026-10-12, sku 43318, change_source customer, removal_reason customer_request, machine `41944cd7-…` (VendPoint Carousel 90, VP-418204).

- New bin: B-03-04, which has no entry in the bin history today.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone
**Root.** The customer's ask, "stocked today", is the placing of opening consigned stock. Per "Opening Consigned Stock in a New Consigned Bin", the book-the-line tool is `stock_opening_consignment_2b5b5df3`.

**Prerequisite sentences on that hub:**
- P1: "The opening stock of such a bin is worked out only after its new-bin entry, flagged consigned and carrying its fill-to level, stands in the program's bin history."
- P2: "The opening stock is not placed until the bin's par level entries carry a reorder point above zero."

**Hop A (P1), state-derived.**
- Record: find_vmi_bins shows no entry for B-03-04. The state does not hold.
- Search words: "new-bin entry", "flagged consigned", "fill-to level".
- "Customer Request for a New Consigned Bin Taking Over a VendPoint Item" says: "One filing books a single new-bin entry on the program's bin history … booked as a consigned bin, flagged consigned … with a reorder point of 0".
- That doc also says: "The request is the customer's own act" and "the customer themselves runs it".
- So the write is the customer's request, handed over by the agent.

**Hop B (P2), state-derived.**
- After hop A, the only entry of B-03-04 carries reorder point 0, because the request "names no reorder point". The state still does not hold.
- Search words: "reorder point", "par level entry".
- "Corbett's Reorder Point Entry for a New Consigned Bin" says Corbett "records that bin's reorder point … as a par level entry that keeps the bin consigned".
- That doc's own sentence: "Corbett's reorder point for such a bin is recorded only after the customer's new-bin entry for it, flagged consigned, stands in the program's bin history."
- So hop B also waits on hop A.

**Order:** customer request, then Corbett reorder-point entry, then the opening-stock line.

**Hop marks.** A is state-derived. B is state-derived. B→A is state-derived from the reorder-point doc's own sentence. No hop was pre-solved:
- no document names another problem's tool;
- the hub names only its own tool;
- the request doc names only its own tool.

**Counter-proof, "do only what was asked" (book stock now).**
- P1 and P2 forbid it on the visible records: no B-03-04 entry, and no par entry with a reorder point above 0.
- Opening Stock Section 1 also leaves no fill-to and no reorder point to compute.
- Booking without the request would also need a bin the customer never asked for in writing. "Bin changes on request … the customer asks".

**Closest alternatives excluded:**
- The Locker 24 vends: excluded by "vends, returns and credits at any other machine are not counted".
- "Takes effect at the next visit": the booking doc says a bin of this kind "takes effect at the program's service visit of the day its entries stand … every other bin change still takes effect from the next visit or scan". bin_changes marks the old words retired.
- Rounding the opening stock up: the standard says "rounded down".
- Consigned price versus list: "at the item's contract unit price".

**Calculation fall-back (no factor applied):**
- Fill-to 122/13 × 2 = 18.769231, so 19.
- Reorder point 1.340659 × 4.75 = 6.368132, so 7.
- Opening stock = fill-to 19.

These are definite and differ from 28 / 19 / 14.

### 7. Open point found blind (candidate defect)
The document "Annual Usage Value Share for Consigned Bins Taking Over VendPoint Items" does not say which carried share it feeds. Both the fill-to level standard (3.3) and the opening-stock standard (Section 3) have a "carried share, which is the product of every share that applies". The doc's only scope sentence reads: "A new consigned bin … carries less Corbett-owned stock when the item is of high annual value", and its table says "Value-class share put into the carried share".

The other share documents name their target:
- "carried share of that bin's fill-to level" (returned payments);
- "Applies to: opening consigned stock" (return rate, credit room, site age, supply share).

Its tier on this world: 167 net units × 6.85 = 1143.95, which is ≥ 1000.00, so **0.9**. The tier fires, and the placement changes scored numbers:

| Reading | Fill-to | Reorder-point entry `max_qty` | Opening stock |
|---|---|---|---|
| (i) feeds the opening-stock carried share ("Corbett-owned stock", Inventory Finance genre) — my primary reading | 28 | 28 | 0.5×(19+28)×0.557685 = 13.105598, so 13 |
| (ii) feeds the fill-to level's carried share ("A new consigned bin … carries") | 13.961538×2.5×0.72 = 25.130769, so 26 | 26 | 0.5×(19+26)×0.61965 = 13.942125, so 13 |
| not applied | 28 | 28 | 14 |

Primary blind answer: fill-to **28**, reorder point **19**, opening stock **13**, unit price 6.8500, visit VV-417530. I record reading (ii) as a reasonable alternative that the visible text does not exclude.

### KB-RUNTIME RED — K1

**Symptom.** A blind reader seeing only the visible corpus put the annual-usage value-class share into the opening-stock carried share. That computed request `max_qty` 28 and reorder-point-entry `max_qty` 28 against gold 26. The alternative placement (fill-to), which gives gold, was equally available, and no visible sentence decides between them.

**Root cause.** In the source, the abc_share factor belongs to vmi_ext_vended_item_fill_level (`decides: abc_share`). Its rule sentence sits inside the fill-to policy's rule: "…puts a value-class share of 0.75 into the carried share…". The factor document drops the policy context that fixes which carried share is meant.

**Evidence (KB).** `docs/vmi/annual_usage_value_share_4f2d4b12.json`:
- title: "StockSmart Inventory Finance Schedule — Annual Usage Value Share for Consigned Bins Taking Over VendPoint Items";
- the only scope sentence: "A new consigned bin … carries less Corbett-owned stock when the item is of high annual value";
- table header: "Value-class share put into the carried share".

Two computation documents each define a "carried share, which is the product of every share that applies":
- `transferred_item_fill_to_level_64087e93.json` 3.2/3.3;
- `opening_consigned_stock_quantity_cb598980.json` Section 3.

Every sibling share document names its target, and this one alone does not:
- `returned_payment_share_37af6788.json`: "the carried share of that bin's fill-to level";
- `machine_return_rate_share_97d37aa6.json` / `receivable_to_limit_credit_room_share_150b112b.json`: "Applies to: opening consigned stock";
- `ship_to_age_site_share_14d0b7d0.json` / `open_backorder_supply_share_9e08bcf6.json`: "For the opening consigned stock".

Its wording "Corbett-owned stock" and its "Inventory Finance" genre (shared with the opening-stock standard) lean toward the wrong placement.

**Effect.** Two equally reasonable formulas for a scored parameter (`max_qty` on both writes). This is the "two equally reasonable formulas" class.

**Not the agent's fault.** The ambiguity is in the visible text. Arithmetic under both readings is recorded above.

**Other items.** Everything else matches the blind answer exactly. No hop was pre-solved.

**Verdict task 0 runtime: KB-RUNTIME RED (K1).**
